recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula or definition you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the logarithmic form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Tanh⁻¹ has its own form, and it carries a HALF outside the logarithm — which is exactly where the 1/2 in the answer comes from.
lines: We know Tanh⁻¹x = (1/2) logₑ((1 + x)/(1 − x))

recall.must_convey: That Tanh⁻¹x = (1/2)logₑ((1+x)/(1−x)) is stated, with the half outside.
accept: tanh inverse x is half log of one plus x over one minus x
state the tanh inverse form with the half outside the log
write the formula for tanh inverse
tanh inverse ki half log one plus x by one minus x
quote the logarithmic form for tanh inverse

steps.why: The 1/2 in the answer is not something to derive — it is part of the formula. Recognising that saves hunting for where it came from.

steps.label: Substitute x = 1/2
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The compound fraction simplifies: (1 + 1/2) over (1 − 1/2) is (3/2) over (1/2), which is 3.

recall.must_convey: That substituting x = 1/2 gives (3/2)/(1/2) = 3, so the answer is (1/2)logₑ3.
accept: substitute a half so it becomes three halves over a half which is three, giving half log three
the answer is half log three
half substitute cheste three vasthundi, so half log three
three halves divided by a half is three

steps.why: Dividing by a half is multiplying by two, which is why (3/2) ÷ (1/2) comes out as a whole number rather than a fraction.
common_mistakes: Getting 3/2 instead of 3 by not dividing properly.
